::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What is meant by the symbol “$\equiv$” in this context?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3338069/what-is-meant-by-the-symbol-equiv-in-this-context), asked by [Lucifer](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/633975/lucifer) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-08-29; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> [![diagram referred to by derivation][q-1]][q-1]
> [![mathematical derivation with confusing statement highlighted][q-2]][q-2]
>
> See the highlighted text in the 2nd photo, where it says
> $$\triangle OAC \equiv \triangle OC'A'$$
> What is meant by the symbol “$\equiv$”?
>
>   [q-1]: gz1Cm.jpg
>   [q-2]: jXoOy.jpg
:::

The symbol $\equiv$ has different meanings in different contexts, but it usually refers to an [equivalence relation][1] distinct from actual equality.

In this context of plane Euclidean geometry, it seems the author is using it for the [congruence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congruence_(geometry)#Congruence_of_triangles) relation on polygons.


  [1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equivalence_relation
